2609.17434.title: CareMirror: Bringing Caregiver Wellbeing into the Dementia Care Ecosystem
2609.17434.paper_summary: Family caregivers of people living with dementia shoulder emotional and practical responsibilities, yet their own wellbeing often remains peripheral to dementia care. We built CareMirror, an envisioned caregiver wellbeing ecosystem with interconnected caregiver- and clinician-facing interfaces for longitudinal reflection, personalized support, and caregiver-controlled sharing with clinical care. We conducted semi-structured interviews with 14 caregivers, using CareMirror as a design probe to examine how they perceived this ecosystem and what expectations, concerns, and boundaries emerged around clinical connection. Caregivers valued attention to their wellbeing, longitudinal awareness, context-sensitive support, and clinical visibility when it could lead to meaningful follow-up. However, repeated reflection could become burdensome or emotionally difficult, automatic clinical sharing could inhibit candid disclosure, and participants wanted control over what information entered clinical care. They also expected AI to support reflection and communication without replacing caregiver voice or clinician judgment. We contribute design considerations for proactive, clinically connected caregiver wellbeing support.
2609.17434.paper_summary_zh: 家庭照顧者在照顧患有癡呆症的人時，承擔著情感和實際的責任，但他們自己的福祉往往在癡呆症護理中處於邊緣地位。<lb/>我們建立了CareMirror，一個設想中的照顧者福祉生態系統，擁有互聯的面向照顧者和臨床醫生的界面，用於長期反思、個性化支持和照顧者控制的臨床共享。<lb/>我們對14位照顧者進行了半結構化訪談，使用CareMirror作為設計探針，檢視他們對這個生態系統的看法，以及圍繞臨床聯繫出現的期望、擔憂和界限。<lb/>照顧者重視對他們福祉的關注、長期的認知、情境敏感的支持，以及在能夠導致有意義的後續跟進時的臨床可見性。<lb/>然而，重複的反思可能會變得繁重或情感上困難，自動的臨床共享可能會抑制坦誠的披露，參與者希望能控制進入臨床護理的信息。<lb/>他們還期望人工智慧能支持反思和溝通，而不取代照顧者的聲音或臨床醫生的判斷。<lb/>我們提供了主動、臨床連結的照顧者福祉支持的設計考量。
